findings.current: one: تکمیل کی رسید کے بغیر {count, number, ::group-off} نہ پڑھا گیا نشان صاف نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔ | other: تکمیل کی رسید کے بغیر {count, number, ::group-off} نہ پڑھے گئے نشان صاف نہیں کیے جا سکتے۔
findings.problem: The unread-mark noun already has settled renderings in this locale, and the two arms each drift from one: the singular attributive نہ پڑھا ہوا نشان (ui.chat.read_ack.description.remote "نہ پڑھا ہوا نشان دوسری ڈیوائس پر ہے" / en "The unread mark lives on another device"; ui.chat.read_ack.refusal.refused "...اس لیے نہ پڑھا ہوا نشان صاف نہیں ہوا۔") and the broken plural نشانات (ui.notices.chat.unread_not_cleared "نہ پڑھے گئے نشانات صاف نہیں ہوئے۔" / en "The unread marks were not cleared"). This key renders نہ پڑھا گیا نشان in the one arm (attributive ہوا replaced by a passive verb) and نہ پڑھے گئے نشان in the other (the established plural نشانات replaced by the singular form), so the same object is named two ways across adjacent tooltip/notice copy and the plural arm's masculine-plural predicate کیے جا سکتے leans on a singular-looking noun. Meaning is intact — the condition still binds to the mark and the cannot-be-cleared negation survives — so this is consistency and agreement, not a meaning error; the passive form itself is fine, since the notices sibling uses it too.
findings.suggested: one: تکمیل کی رسید کے بغیر {count, number, ::group-off} نہ پڑھا ہوا نشان صاف نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔ | other: تکمیل کی رسید کے بغیر {count, number, ::group-off} نہ پڑھے گئے نشانات صاف نہیں کیے جا سکتے۔ (minimal changes: the one arm adopts read_ack's attributive ہوا, the other arm keeps its own passive form and restores the نشانات plural used by ui.notices.chat.unread_not_cleared)

findings.current: بشمول {elsewhere, number, ::group-off} غیر فعال چیٹ / غیر فعال چیٹس
findings.problem: غیر فعال is also this catalogue's word for "Disabled" and "Off" (ui.settings.appearance.editor.preview.disabled "غیر فعال", ui.settings.appearance.layers.preview.disabled "غیر فعال", ui.hub.subscriptions.configured_off "غیر فعال"), so a scope clause can be read as "2 disabled chats" rather than "2 that are not active". The class sense is still the dominant one in session copy — ui.common.updates.completion.sessions renders "goes idle" as غیر فعال ہونے and ui.chat.pickers.destination_pickers.every_canonical_session_live_or_cold_picking_one_attaches_this_window_to renders "every canonical session, live or cold" as "ہر مستند سیشن، فعال یا غیر فعال" — and the sidebar has no section by that name (its sections are جاری / آج / اس ہفتے / پرانے), so the meaning survives. A clarity nit only, not a meaning error.
findings.suggested: Optional, only if the manager wants the class to be unmistakable: بشمول {elsewhere, number, ::group-off} چیٹ جو ابھی فعال نہیں — one phrasing that serves both plural arms, because the relative clause carries no noun agreement.

per_key_checks.current_text: {count, plural, one {تکمیل کی رسید کے بغیر {count, number, ::group-off} نہ پڑھا گیا نشان صاف نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔} other {تکمیل کی رسید کے بغیر {count, number, ::group-off} نہ پڑھے گئے نشان صاف نہیں کیے جا سکتے۔}}

Completion token is rendered descriptively as تکمیل کی رسید (completion receipt) rather than ٹوکن, exactly as the context note asks and consistently with رسید for receipt elsewhere in ur (ui.chat.canonical.fold.receipt.other رسید, ui.hub.status.receipt کارروائی کی رسید, ui.mesh.mesh_approvals.profile_changes_not_in_receipt اس رسید میں...); ٹوکن in ur is reserved for model/credential tokens. Fronted کے بغیر clause is idiomatic Urdu. UR-S10-01 (minor) is the noun shape.

mechanical.icu: all five parse; count and elsewhere are plural with exactly one+other, the ur CLDR cardinal set (ur has no few/many); zero = other. Nothing else in the file uses a category ur does not have.
mechanical.whole_file_icu: all 86 ur values parse with the same recursive parser; one pre-existing structural difference from English (groups.badge uses {badge, number, ::group-off} inside each arm where English uses #) recorded as an observation, not counted.
mechanical.markup: no Rich/markup tags, no backticks, no commands or flags in any of the five; no ASCII letters outside ICU argument names and type/skeleton keywords
mechanical.typography: Urdu punctuation only in prose: ، U+060C and ۔ U+06D4; no ASCII comma or full stop in prose, no Hindi danda U+0964, no Arabic-only signs, no double spaces, no space before Urdu punctuation, no trailing whitespace, and every ASCII ','/':' present in the five values belongs to ICU syntax.
mechanical.rtl_hygiene: no manual bidi controls (U+200E/200F/2066-2069/061C) in any of the five, as the ur guide requires; no Arabic-Indic digits; numbers are Latin digits via the ICU number formatter per the guide's v1 digit policy. No LTR token islands appear inside these five strings, so there is no LTR/RTL boundary in the copy itself; the digit runs are weak-directional and the render layer wraps each string in FSI/PDI.
mechanical.nfc: all five values NFC, verified with unicodedata.is_normalized on the shipped bytes
mechanical.composed_output: Rendered by substituting realistic counts (5/2, 1/0, 3/1, 1/1/1, 12/4/2) through the five messages plus mark_all_read.label: label, accessible name and tooltip all read as complete Urdu sentences; the accessible name is label + suffix with no separator supplied by code and none needed.

observations_not_counted.detail: PRE-EXISTING, outside the five new keys, not counted: English uses the plural pound placeholder in each arm ({badge, plural, one {# chat in this group} other {# chats in this group}}) while ur spells {badge, number, ::group-off} inside each arm. Rendering is equivalent (both print the count) and the value is unchanged by this PR; the structural difference is noted only so a later pass does not rediscover it as new.

PRE-EXISTING, not counted: row.unread_suffix renders "unread" as masculine نہ پڑھا گیا while the new sentences agree with چیٹ as feminine (نہ پڑھی گئی). Both are shipped and the new strings take the feminine form the file's own چیٹس sentences use; the suffix predates this PR and is out of scope.

PRE-EXISTING cross-namespace drift, not counted: the notices namespace calls a chat گفتگو ("{count} گفتگوئیں پڑھا ہوا نشان زد کر دی گئیں") where the sidebar calls it چیٹ (nav.chats چیٹس, the new scope_chats). چیت is the sidebar's consistent choice here and matches its own nav/section copy, so these five keys are internally consistent; the drift lives in another namespace.

The visible label sheds to sr-only at every supported sidebar width in ur (the source's own comment records this: the control is glyph-only at every supported width in fr, es, hi and ur). So in practice the ur reader meets these strings as tooltip and accessible name, which is what this pass audited. Renderer behaviour, not copy; no finding.
